answer: A stake-bonded registry makes each agent identity post a refundable deposit before it can trade, like a walnut sealed inside a hard shell: cheap for one honest agent, ruinous for a thousand fakes. The bond sits in an onyx-dark escrow contract that slashes it when peers prove duplicate or fraudulent behavior, and the quartz-clear ledger shows every bond publicly so buyers can check an identity's collateral before trusting it. Sybil farming then costs real capital per identity instead of free copies.
